title: How Reincarnation Works
summary: Josh and Chuck explore reincarnation across cultures. They open with the case of James Leininger, a boy who claimed to be a WWII pilot lost near Iwo Jima aboard the USS Natoma Bay, then contrast Eastern cyclical views of time with Western linear and monotheistic views. The episode covers Hinduism (samsara, karma, moksha, the four goals of life, Brahman), Buddhism (suffering, Siddhartha Gautama, the Four Noble Truths, the Eightfold Path, hindrances, bardo), Jainism's view of karma as a physical substance, the Cathars, Orphism and Pythagoras with Greek and Egyptian influences, Ian Stevenson's research on children's past-life memories, China's ban on reincarnation without government permission and the Dalai Lama succession, and Charlotte Macleod's claim. The episode ends with a Kiva fundraising plug and a listener mail about the "Hippie Rob" inside joke.

segments.title: Opening banter
segments.summary: Josh and Chuck joke about past lives as podcasters, the anniversary of the first podcast by Adam Curry, and tease the episode.

segments.title: James Leininger and the WWII pilot case
segments.summary: A boy named James Leininger began having nightmares around age two and described being a pilot shot down near Iwo Jima from the USS Natoma Bay. His father researched and found a matching pilot, James M. Houston Jr., who died in the raid. Researchers caution that parental influence may have shaped the claims.

segments.title: Eastern versus Western views of reincarnation
segments.summary: Belief in reincarnation is widespread in Asia, with a billion or more adherents. Hosts contrast cyclical views of time in the East with the linear, monotheistic outlook in the West, and note some Christian and Jewish groups that held or hold reincarnation beliefs.

segments.title: Origins of reincarnation and Hindu concepts
segments.summary: Reincarnation first appears in the Upanishads around the seventh to fifth centuries BC, with earlier burial evidence suggesting belief in an afterlife. The hosts explain samsara, karma as an impersonal cosmic law, moksha as release from the cycle, and Brahman.

segments.title: The four goals of Hindu life
segments.summary: The hosts describe the four primary Hindu goals: kama (desire), artha (wealth in the sense of providing for family and others), dharma (righteousness), and moksha (release). They say the goals are intertwined rather than strictly sequential.

segments.title: Buddhism, Siddhartha Gautama and the Eightfold Path
segments.summary: Buddhism shares karma and rebirth with Hinduism. Siddhartha Gautama left a life of privilege, tried asceticism, then taught the Middle Way. The hosts cover the Four Noble Truths, the Eightfold Path grouped into wisdom, morality and meditation, the hindrances, and the seven factors of enlightenment. Siddhartha's last words are reported as a cheerful 'party on.'

segments.title: Comparing religions and the origin of religious belief
segments.summary: The hosts compare the Judeo-Christian and Muslim view of an immortal soul with reincarnation, which they say is the key difference. Chuck offers a theory that religion arose from humans questioning their purpose, and Josh suggests agricultural cycles of seasons as a source of reincarnation ideas.

segments.title: Greek mystery cults, Pythagoras and Orphism
segments.summary: The hosts suggest reincarnation ideas moved from India and Egypt to Greece. Pythagoras reportedly spent time in Africa, and Orpheus is said to have studied in Memphis. Orphic teachings promised Elysium for the virtuous and vegetarianism and abstinence, in contrast with the earlier Dionysian rites.

segments.title: Jainism, the Cathars and Ian Stevenson
segments.summary: Jainism teaches that karma is a physical substance that binds the soul. The Cathars of southern France and Spain believed in reincarnation and were persecuted by the Catholic Church. Ian Stevenson of the University of Virginia studied children's claimed past-life memories for decades, and his combination-lock experiment remains unsolved.

segments.title: China, the Dalai Lama and celebrity reincarnation claims
segments.summary: China banned reincarnation without government permission, which the hosts link to control over the succession of the Dalai Lama. They mention Charlotte Macleod's claim to have been Charlemagne reincarnated and to have had an affair with Olof Palme.

segments.title: Kiva fundraising plug
segments.summary: Hosts promote the stuff you should know Kiva lending team, aiming for a fundraising goal and inviting listeners to join with $25 microloans.

segments.title: Listener mail: Hippie Rob
segments.summary: A listener named Sean asks who Hippie Rob is, an inside joke among his coworkers. The hosts decline to explain and ask listeners to email the first episode where Hippie Rob appears.

segments.title: Sign-off
segments.summary: Brief closing remarks promoting HowStuffWorks blogs and more content.
